findings.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:303 — Starting the watcher after the search index build creates an event-loss window, leaving writes committed during initialization missing from the index until modified again

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Unconditionally skipping the PostgreSQL integration test in CI removes coverage of eager initialization and allows PostgreSQL-specific startup regressions to go undetected

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:303 — Starting the watcher after the search index build creates an event-loss window, leaving writes committed during initialization missing from the index until modified again

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the order of initialization was changed: previously initWatcher() was called before s.search.init(ctx), but now s.search.init(ctx) is called first (lines 303-305), then initWatcher() is called after (lines 308-310). The search index initialization reads existing data from storage, but if the watcher isn't started until after the index is built, any writes that occur during the index building process would be missed. These events would not be captured by the watcher (not started yet) and would not be in the initial index snapshot (already committed before the read). This is a real race condition that could cause data inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Unconditionally skipping the PostgreSQL integration test in CI removes coverage of eager initialization and allows PostgreSQL-specific startup regressions to go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new test skip being added for PostgreSQL with a TODO comment indicating the test doesn't work in Drone CI but works locally. This is a legitimate concern - the PR introduces eager initialization changes (moving Init() call to NewResourceServer and reordering initialization), and skipping the PostgreSQL integration test means these changes won't be validated against PostgreSQL in CI. The finding correctly identifies that this reduces test coverage for the new initialization behavior specifically for PostgreSQL, which could allow regressions to slip through.
